facts.text: Horsfield's bronze cuckoo averages 22 grams and shows green and bronze iridescent colouring on its back.
facts.quote: Its size averages 22 g (0.78 oz) and is distinguished by its green and bronze iridescent colouring on its back and incomplete brown barring from neck to tail.

facts.text: You can tell it from other bronze cuckoos by its white eyebrow and brown eye stripe.
facts.quote: Horsfield's bronze cuckoo can be distinguished from other bronze cuckoos by its white eyebrow and brown eye stripe.

facts.text: It is common throughout Australia, preferring drier open woodlands away from forested areas.
facts.quote: The Horsfield's bronze cuckoo is common throughout Australia preferring the drier open woodlands away from forested areas.

facts.text: It eats mainly insects, snatching them from leaves and branches or catching them on the wing.
facts.quote: Small insects are taken from leaves, branches, caught on the wing and in breeding season, Horsfield's bronze cuckoos feed each other in a courtship ritual.

facts.text: During breeding season, courting cuckoos feed each other.
facts.quote: in breeding season, Horsfield's bronze cuckoos feed each other in a courtship ritual.

facts.text: It is a brood parasite that lays its eggs mainly in the nests of fairy-wrens, letting them raise its young.
facts.quote: The Horsfield's bronze cuckoo is known as a brood parasite, this means that they lay their eggs in a host species nest. They mainly parasitize the fairy-wrens in the genus Malurus.

facts.text: Its egg mimics the fairy-wren or thornbill egg, being elongated, pinkish-white and speckled with red-brown spots.
facts.quote: they will lay one to mimic that of the fairy wren or thornbill's egg, an elongated pinkish-white egg, that is speckled with red-brown spots.

facts.text: The female can lay an egg in under six seconds, usually in the morning shortly after the host has laid.
facts.quote: Egg laying is very fast for the Horsfield's bronze cuckoo; it is able to lay an egg in under 6 seconds typically in the morning shortly after the host has laid.

facts.text: The chick hatches within 12 days, two days before the host's eggs, and ejects the other eggs from the nest.
facts.quote: The cuckoo chick hatches within 12 days of incubation, 2 days before the host egg, ejecting other eggs in the nests within two days of hatching, leaving the cuckoo the sole chick.

facts.text: In 2024, the first known specimen was recorded in New Zealand.
facts.quote: In 2024, the first known specimen was recorded in New Zealand.
